title: The Good Samaritan
review_status: DRAFT: retelling and wondering questions require theological and editorial review before release.

source.note: Original child-friendly retelling written for this prototype; not a quotation of any translation.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: This is a story Jesus told. Let's carry the story box to the table, and listen.

segments.text: One day, a man asked Jesus, "Who is my neighbor?" Jesus answered by telling a story.
A man was walking along the road, down from Jerusalem toward Jericho.
On the way, some robbers took his things and hurt him. They left him by the side of the road.
A priest, who served at God's house, came down the same road. He saw the hurt man, but he walked past on the other side.
Then a Levite, another helper at God's house, came by. He looked at the man, and he walked past on the other side, too.
Then a man from Samaria came by with his donkey. His people and the hurt man's people were not friends. But when he saw the hurt man, he felt very sorry for him.
He knelt down and put bandages on the man's hurts. He lifted him onto his donkey and took him to an inn, a house where travelers sleep. There he looked after him.
The next day, he gave the innkeeper two coins and said, "Please look after him. If you need more, I will pay you when I come back."
Then Jesus asked, "Which one was a neighbor to the hurt man?" The man said, "The one who was kind to him." And Jesus said, "Go and do the same."

wonderings: I wonder how the man felt when the Samaritan stopped to help him.
I wonder what the Samaritan was thinking when he stopped.
I wonder who is a neighbor.
I wonder who might need a neighbor near you.
